Question B-006-010-001.

Why the correct answer is right: The exam-style quarter-wave estimate for HF verticals uses length in metres ≈ 71.3 / frequency in MHz.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "Divide 71.3 by the operating frequency in MHz": Correct. 71.3 divided by frequency in MHz is the quarter-wave vertical estimate used here.
- sourceIndex 1: "Divide 468 by the operating frequency in MHz": 468/f is a feet-based half-wave dipole shortcut, not the metre quarter-wave estimate.
- sourceIndex 2: "Divide 300 by the operating frequency in MHz": 300/f gives full free-space wavelength in metres, not the shortened quarter-wave antenna length.
- sourceIndex 3: "Divide 143 by the operating frequency in MHz": 143/f gives an approximate half-wave length in metres, not a quarter-wave length.
